body: LeBron James recorded his first triple-double as a member of the 76ers on Wednesday, Nov. 25, with 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds in a 111-104 NBA Cup win over the Miami Heat at Xfinity Mobile Arena. He shot 9-for-15, made four of his six threes and finished plus-14.
The signature stretch came in the first half, when James scored 14 points in a row to push Philadelphia ahead 47-39.
## Why fans are buying in

The timing made the night bigger. Joel Embiid sat out with an illness for a second straight game, and Jaylen Brown left at halftime with hamstring tightness, so James carried the offense alongside Tyrese Maxey, who scored 30. The win, which moved the Sixers to 15-4, also came two nights after a lopsided loss in Portland.

Then there is the history. James signed with Philadelphia in July 2026, opened a record 24th NBA season in October and turns 42 on Dec. 30. In our analysis, every big night now doubles as a chance to see one of the game's all-time greats in a new uniform, and that is exactly the kind of moment fans want a jersey to mark.

body: Blake Corum had the best game of his NFL career on Wednesday, Nov. 25, rushing 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown as the Los Angeles Rams beat the Green Bay Packers 26-13 at SoFi Stadium. It was also his 26th birthday.
He did most of it after halftime, with 25 carries for 161 yards in the second half as the Rams kept the ball away from Green Bay.
## Why fans are buying in

This is a breakout, not a one-off, and the numbers back it up. Corum has now scored a touchdown in seven straight games, and his 32 carries were the most by a Rams running back in a game since Todd Gurley in 2015.

His role has grown at the right moment. With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both injured, Sean McVay has leaned on the run, and the Rams piled up 241 rushing yards while winning a fifth game in a row. At 7-4, they are right back in the NFC playoff race.

Fans already knew the name. Corum was a national champion at Michigan before the Rams drafted him with the 83rd pick in 2024. In our analysis, a former college star turning into a workhorse back is exactly the kind of story that builds a following for a jersey.
## The look
Corum wears No. 24. The banner above shows the Rams' royal blue home jersey and the white road jersey. The Rams also debuted their Fearsome White throwback uniforms in this game.
## Why this jersey will last

Running backs who carry an offense in December tend to become fan favorites, and Corum is doing it on a winning team in a big market. The Rams host Kansas City on Thursday, Dec. 3, a national stage for another big night.

body: Deni Avdija scored 33 points, with 12 rebounds and seven assists, as the Portland Trail Blazers beat the San Antonio Spurs 116-111 at the Moda Center on Wednesday, Nov. 25. He shot 11-for-21, including 5-for-8 from three.
He outscored everyone on his side on a night when Victor Wembanyama put up 44 points and 16 rebounds for San Antonio.
## Why fans are buying in

The win mattered in the standings. Portland moved to 12-6 and 2-1 in NBA Cup group play, keeping its hopes alive for a wild-card spot in the knockout round, and it came against one of the best teams in the West. Damian Lillard added 29 and Sidy Cissoko scored 16, giving the Blazers a two-man punch that can beat anyone on a good night.

Avdija has grown into the player Portland builds around. He averaged 24.2 points, 6.9 rebounds and 6.7 assists over 66 games in 2025-26, and in February 2026 he became the first Israeli player ever named an NBA All-Star. In our analysis, that mix of all-around production and a global following makes his jersey one with fans well beyond Oregon.
Nights like this one show why. He scored from deep, got to the line and owned the defensive glass with 10 of his 12 rebounds, the kind of complete, two-way game that wins over a whole fan base.

## Why this jersey will last

Avdija is 25, an All-Star still in his prime and the clear centerpiece of a team climbing back into the playoff picture. Portland hosts Golden State on Friday in its final group-stage game, with a knockout spot still in reach.
